newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Alrenco defends Q4 writeoffs.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Alrenco defends Q4 writeoffs.

text.p: Alrenco Inc's chief financial officer on Friday defended the company's decision to take certain writeoffs in the fourth quarter, even though the news knocked 39.7 percent from the value of its stock.
"We are accelerating some expenditures into the fourth quarter to take advantage of the holiday buying season. It's a sound business decision," said Theodore Wilson in a telephone interview.
But Wilson conceded, "The market reaction will dampen our ability to use stock in (future) acquisitions."

Stock of New Albany, Ind.-based Alrenco, which operates rental-purchase stores in the Southeast, Midwest and mid-Atlantic region, dropped 7-1/2 to 12 after the company said it would post fourth-quarter earnings even with or slightly below year-ago earnings of $0.16 per share.
"We have adequate reserves -- cash and bank loan availability -- to do acquisitions going forward," Wilson said.
Since its initial public offering last January, Alrenco has added 71 stores, all through acquisitions, bringing its total to 124 units.
"In 1997, we are looking at potentially adding 35 to 40 stores, through a combination of acquisition and startup," Wilson said.
He said some stores acquired in the past year, primarily in Atlanta, have not performed as well as anticipated.

Alrenco was boosting advertising expenditures to take advantage of strong rental-purchase activity during the holiday season. It also plans to write off distressed merchandise, and will overstaff and increase supervision at certain acquired outlets.
"These actions will make us a stronger company as we enter 1997," Wilson noted, adding "The (company's) fundamentals have not changed."
